key_insight: Ex vivo adenomyosis tissue showed similar basal contractions to controls, but 1.8-fold higher oxytocin receptor density and a smaller oxytocin-induced increase in contraction frequency.
clinical_relevance: These findings inform research into altered uterine oxytocin signaling in adenomyosis, without establishing implications for diagnosis or treatment.
method: Prospective ex vivo case-control study of hysterectomy tissue from premenopausal women.
Video-based spatiotemporal mapping measured contractions across the myometrium before and after oxytocin.
Immunofluorescence with machine learning-assisted segmentation quantified oxytocin receptor density.
evidence_signal: The study enrolled 16 adenomyosis patients and 12 controls; contractility analysis used 57 strips from 11 versus 8 patients, and immunofluorescence included 10 versus 9 patients.
watch_item: Small, ex vivo hysterectomy cohorts limit generalizability to uterine activity in vivo, and the abstract provides no validation metrics for the machine learning-assisted segmentation.
paper_title: Spatiotemporal mapping of ex vivo myometrial contractions in adenomyosis
